meta.storyTitle: insrc_present cannot show a tracked-epic artifact when code review is unavailable

summary.prose: Corrects three gaps a manual code review found in the already-built fix: the VS Code chat extension's own copy of the presentability check still reads the old pending-only list, so the MCP tool can report a document as presented while the editor pane still refuses to open it; the new daemon-side scanner (resolveOpenableArtifacts) derives a BUILD or AMD record's document path without the existing safety checks that keep a dead or wrong path out of the list; and the registered insrc_present tool description still describes the old, lifecycle-gated behavior. This correction wires the VS Code client to the same openable list the daemon already serves, extracts the existing per-kind path rules into one shared helper so both scanners use them, and updates the tool description's wording.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: insrc_present cannot show a tracked-epic artifact when code review is unavailable

api.name: openableDocuments
api.signature: openableDocuments(): Promise<Array<{ readonly id: string; readonly mdPath: string }>>

returns.meaning: Every PENDING_KINDS artifact the daemon's workflow.openable answers, regardless of lifecycle status -- the client-side twin of resolveOpenableArtifacts, added to DocsReviewClient (vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts) beside the existing pendingDocuments().

errors.condition: the daemon is unreachable or answers a structured { error } -- propagated exactly as pendingDocuments() already propagates workflow.pending's failures.

preconditions: A repo path is resolvable (the same repo() option pendingDocuments() already uses).
postconditions: Resolves to the daemon's workflow.openable artifacts unchanged; makes no daemon write call.

api.name: mdPathForKind
api.signature: function mdPathForKind(repoPath: string, kind: PendingKind, artifactId: string, meta: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): string

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The repo root to resolve the document path inside.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.purpose: Which artifact kind's path rule to apply.

parameters.name: artifactId
parameters.purpose: The exact artifact id a BUILD.md's marker comment must carry for that file to count as this record's document.

parameters.name: meta
parameters.purpose: The artifact's meta, passed through to deriveMdPath.

returns.meaning: '' for AMD; buildRecordMdPath's existence+marker-checked result for BUILD; deriveMdPath's result for every other kind. Extracted from toDescriptor's existing inline branching so toDescriptor and resolveOpenableArtifacts share one definition.

postconditions: toDescriptor and resolveOpenableArtifacts both call this instead of each deciding the per-kind rule inline.

api.name: resolveOpenableArtifacts

returns.meaning: Reshaped only internally: mdPath now comes from mdPathForKind(repoPath, kind, artifactId, art.meta) instead of a direct deriveMdPath call, so a BUILD entry's path is '' unless the file exists and carries this record's marker, and an AMD entry's path is always ''.

postconditions: Every returned BUILD path is file-existence- and marker-verified; every returned AMD path is ''; every other kind is unchanged.

api.name: toDescriptor
api.signature: function toDescriptor(repoPath: string, file: string, kind: PendingKind, art: ArtifactShape): PendingArtifact

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The repo the artifact file lives in.

returns.meaning: Unchanged descriptor shape; its mdPath field now comes from the shared mdPathForKind instead of an inline ternary -- same values, same behavior, single source.

postconditions: listPendingArtifacts' own tests (pending/approved/rejected filtering, the BUILD/CR-sibling gate) keep passing unmodified: this is a pure refactor of toDescriptor's path derivation, not a behavior change.

errorCases.scenario: openableDocuments() daemon round-trip fails (unreachable daemon or a structured { error } from workflow.openable)
errorCases.detection: The same IpcClient rejection / structured-error path pendingDocuments() already uses for workflow.pending -- no new detection logic.
errorCases.response: Propagated as a thrown Error, exactly as pendingDocuments() propagates a workflow.pending failure today; review-presenter's existing catch in read() sets outcome.unreadable = true and logs a warning.
errorCases.userImpact: The turn's declared documents are reported unreadable and nothing opens -- identical to today's failure mode for pendingDocuments(), just reached via a different method name.

errorCases.scenario: mdPathForKind is asked for a BUILD record whose BUILD.md is missing, or exists but does not carry THIS record's exact artifact marker
errorCases.detection: buildRecordMdPath's existing existsSync check and `<!-- insrc:artifact <id> -->` substring check, now reached through mdPathForKind instead of toDescriptor's inline call.
errorCases.response: Returns '' (document-less); the record is still openable by artifact id.
errorCases.userImpact: No change from today's listPendingArtifacts behavior for the same BUILD record -- resolveOpenableArtifacts now matches it exactly instead of returning a dead or wrong path.

errorCases.scenario: mdPathForKind is asked for an AMD record
errorCases.detection: An explicit kind === 'AMD' branch, unconditional -- no file-system check at all (an amendment is JSON-only).
errorCases.userImpact: The amendment is openable by artifact id, exactly as listPendingArtifacts already presents it; resolveOpenableArtifacts stops fabricating a nonexistent AMD.md path.

edgeCases.input: A repo with zero PENDING_KINDS artifact files.
edgeCases.expected: openableDocuments() and resolveOpenableArtifacts both return []; review-presenter reports every declared name as notPending -- unchanged from today's behavior for an empty/absent store.

edgeCases.input: A BUILD.md on disk whose marker comment names a DIFFERENT artifactId than the record being resolved (a stale or superseded file).
edgeCases.expected: mdPathForKind returns '' for this record, never the other record's path -- the marker check is exact-match, not existence-only.

edgeCases.input: The JetBrains plugin's own review panel, reading the SAME repo at the same time via its own daemon IPC call to workflow.pending.
edgeCases.expected: Fully unaffected: it is a different client, a different call, and this Story does not touch it or listPendingArtifacts.

invariantsToPreserve.text: createReviewPresenter's only production wiring point is extension.ts's activate() (lines 104-1090, wiring at 730-734); openableDocuments must be wired at that exact call site with no other caller introduced, since the analyze bundle and a direct grep both found no second VS Code consumer of the pending/openable list.

toDescriptor's BUILD path is '' unless the derived BUILD.md exists AND its head carries this record's exact `<!-- insrc:artifact <id> -->` marker (buildRecordMdPath, pending.ts:259-276); mdPathForKind must preserve this check exactly, not approximate it with an existence-only test.
toDescriptor's AMD path is always '' (pending.ts:238-240) because an amendment is a JSON record with no rendered document; mdPathForKind must preserve this unconditional empty-path rule exactly.

The registered insrc_present tool description (server.ts:870-895) must state that presentation is independent of lifecycle status, matching handleInsrcPresent's actual openableWorkflow-backed behavior: an already-approved or already-rejected artifact is presented, not notPending.

testLevels.purpose: Prove openableDocuments() forwards to workflow.openable (not workflow.pending) and propagates a daemon failure exactly like pendingDocuments() does.
fixturesNeeded: a fake daemon/IpcClient stand-in recording the method name it was called with, mirroring the existing pendingDocuments() test fixture

testLevels.purpose: Prove review-presenter's declared() auto-open path is now driven by the openable list, so an approved/rejected document is opened, not refused.
fixturesNeeded: the existing kit() fixture in review-presenter.test.ts, fed an openable-shaped PendingDocument list including an entry that would have been excluded under the old pending-only semantics

testLevels.purpose: Prove mdPathForKind reproduces toDescriptor's exact existing per-kind rules: BUILD file-existence + marker check, AMD unconditional empty string, every other kind via deriveMdPath unchanged.
fixturesNeeded: the existing pending.test.ts fixtureRepo() helper; a BUILD.md with a matching marker, one missing, one with a mismatched marker; an AMD record

testLevels.purpose: Prove resolveOpenableArtifacts now returns '' for a missing/mismatched BUILD.md and for every AMD record, closing the gap the manual review found.
fixturesNeeded: the same fixtureRepo() fixtures as the mdPathForKind tests

testLevels.purpose: Confirm the registered insrc_present tool description text states presentation is lifecycle-status-independent and no longer claims an approved artifact is notPending.

provingTests: DocsReviewClient.openableDocuments calls the daemon's 'workflow.openable' method, not 'workflow.pending'
review-presenter declared() opens a document that is approved/rejected/has no CR sibling when its source list is openable-shaped, where the old pending-only fixture would have refused it
mdPathForKind returns '' for a BUILD record whose BUILD.md is missing
mdPathForKind returns '' for a BUILD record whose BUILD.md exists but carries a different record's marker
mdPathForKind returns the derived path for a BUILD record whose BUILD.md exists and carries its own marker
mdPathForKind returns '' for every AMD record, unconditionally
resolveOpenableArtifacts returns '' for a BUILD record with no matching BUILD.md
resolveOpenableArtifacts returns '' for an AMD record
toDescriptor's existing listPendingArtifacts tests still pass unmodified after the mdPathForKind extraction

the registered insrc_present description no longer contains the phrase 'pending approval and openable' or lists an approved artifact under notPending's examples, and instead states presentation is independent of lifecycle status

migration.stateBefore: Per c1: vscode-plugin's DocsReviewClient.pendingDocuments() calls workflow.pending, and extension.ts:730-734 wires it as review-presenter.ts's sole pendingDocuments dependency, so the VS Code chat's auto-open flow still applies the pending-only/BUILD-CR-sibling gate the daemon side of this Story already removed for the MCP tool. Per c2: resolveOpenableArtifacts calls deriveMdPath uniformly, bypassing toDescriptor's existing buildRecordMdPath existence/marker check and AMD empty-path sentinel. Per c3: server.ts's registered insrc_present description still states the pre-fix, lifecycle-gated semantics.
migration.stateAfter: DocsReviewClient gains openableDocuments() (calls workflow.openable); extension.ts:732 wires review-presenter's pendingDocuments dependency to it instead of pendingDocuments(). pending.ts gains a shared mdPathForKind helper carrying toDescriptor's exact BUILD/AMD rules; both toDescriptor and resolveOpenableArtifacts call it. server.ts's insrc_present description states presentation is independent of lifecycle status.

migrationSteps.action: Add mdPathForKind(repoPath, kind, artifactId, meta) to src/workflow/pending.ts, extracting toDescriptor's existing BUILD/AMD branching verbatim (no behavior change).
Change toDescriptor to call mdPathForKind instead of its inline ternary; change resolveOpenableArtifacts to call mdPathForKind instead of calling deriveMdPath directly.
Add openableDocuments() to DocsReviewClient (vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts), mirroring pendingDocuments()'s shape but forwarding to workflow.openable.
Change extension.ts:732's reviewPresenter pendingDocuments dependency to call reviewClient.openableDocuments() instead of reviewClient.pendingDocuments().
Reword the registered insrc_present tool description in server.ts to state presentation is independent of lifecycle status, removing the 'already approved' notPending example.

migration.backwardCompat: pendingDocuments() and workflow.pending stay exactly as they are -- the JetBrains review panel and any other caller of pendingDocuments() keep today's pending-only semantics unchanged. No field, method or IPC message is removed; openableDocuments() is purely additive on the client, mirroring the daemon side's existing additive openableWorkflow. toDescriptor's output is bit-for-bit unchanged (pure refactor via mdPathForKind), so listPendingArtifacts' own tests need no change.

alternativesConsidered.name: Full correction: client-side openable twin + shared path-rule helper + description fix
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add openableDocuments() to DocsReviewClient (mirrors pendingDocuments, calls workflow.openable), rewire review-presenter's dependency to it, extract toDescriptor's per-kind mdPath rules into a shared helper both it and resolveOpenableArtifacts call, and correct the insrc_present tool description.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Three independent, additive corrections, each mirroring an existing pattern: (1) vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts gains openableDocuments() (same shape as pendingDocuments, forwards to workflow.openable instead of workflow.pending); vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts:732 rewires reviewPresenter's pendingDocuments dependency to call it. (2) src/workflow/pending.ts extracts a shared mdPathForKind(repoPath, kind, artifactId, meta) helper from toDescriptor's existing BUILD/AMD special-casing (buildRecordMdPath + '' sentinel) and both toDescriptor and resolveOpenableArtifacts call it, so the two scanners can never again diverge on path-derivation correctness. (3) server.ts's insrc_present description is reworded to state presentation is independent of lifecycle status.
pros: Each fix is additive/mirrors an already-reviewed pattern (openableWorkflow already mirrors pendingWorkflow daemon-side) -- minimal new design risk
Closes the HIGH-severity end-to-end gap: the MCP tool's presented answer and the VS Code editor's actual open behavior agree again
Single source of truth for per-kind path rules removes the exact class of bug the reviewer found, not just today's instance of it
listPendingArtifacts / pendingDocuments / the JetBrains review panel keep their narrower pending-only semantics untouched
cons: Touches vscode-plugin/, outside the Plan's original 4-task surface -- requires a new Task and a VS Code extension test
Three unrelated-looking edits in one Story; must keep each one's scope tight so a reviewer can tell them apart

alternativesConsidered.name: Partial: fix only pending.ts's path rules + the tool description
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the original LLD's 'leave all IDE consumers untouched' decision; only fix resolveOpenableArtifacts' path derivation and the stale tool description.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Apply (2) and (3) from a1 but skip (1): do not touch vscode-plugin. The daemon-side scanner and the MCP tool description become correct, but the VS Code chat UI's own pendingDocuments() call is left reading workflow.pending.
pros: Smallest possible diff -- stays entirely inside the already-approved Plan's file surface
Fixes two of the three reviewer findings with no new Task
cons: Does NOT fix the HIGH-severity finding: insrc_present would still report presented while the VS Code editor pane refuses to open the document -- the reported defect's end-to-end symptom survives for VS Code users
Repeats the exact mistake the review caught: assuming an IDE consumer that is a documented 'twin' of server-side logic can be left out of a server-side behavior change
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates the HIGH-severity finding by design: leaves the VS Code auto-open path on workflow.pending, so the MCP tool would keep reporting presented while the editor pane refuses to open the document.

alternativesConsidered.name: Widen pendingDocuments() itself in place
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Change DocsReviewClient.pendingDocuments() to call workflow.openable directly, with no new method and no rename.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Since the analyze bundle (usage.example on createReviewPresenter) and a direct grep both found no other VS Code consumer of pendingDocuments()/workflow.pending, redefine pendingDocuments() in place to call workflow.openable, forwarding the result unchanged.
pros: No new method name to introduce or wire
Slightly smaller diff than a1's client-side half
cons: The method is still literally named pendingDocuments while it would return lifecycle-independent (including approved/rejected) results -- misleading to any future reader or second consumer

A future genuine VS Code 'pending-approvals' feature (mirroring the JetBrains review panel) would have to re-split this method later, repeating work a1 avoids by naming the two concerns separately from the start

Breaks DocsReviewClient's own interface contract comment ('pending()' -> 'workflow.pending') without updating it, reintroducing the same kind of stale-description drift Finding 3 just caught server-side
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally closes the HIGH gap but via a misleadingly-named method (pendingDocuments would return lifecycle-independent results) and an unmaintained interface-contract comment, and does not itself address the MED/LOW findings.

alternativesConsidered.name: Invert control: insrc_present's own response carries the open targets
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Stop having review-presenter poll a separate pendingDocuments()/openableDocuments() list at all; have the chat host open documents directly from insrc_present's tool-call result.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Change the chat-host/provider-mapper protocol so the declared documents and their resolved mdPaths travel on the insrc_present tool-call event itself, and review-presenter opens from that payload instead of making its own daemon round-trip.
pros: Eliminates the whole class of client/server drift this review found, permanently -- there would be only one source of truth for 'what did insrc_present just decide'
Removes a full daemon round-trip from the auto-open path
cons: A protocol change across the chat-host, provider-mapper and both extension clients (VS Code + any future consumer) -- far beyond a bugfix Story's scope
No existing design covers this; it would need its own Epic/HLD, not a Story-level LLD correction
Changes behavior unrelated to the three reviewer findings (which are all fixable without touching the tool-call protocol)
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: An unscoped, oversized protocol change across the chat-host/provider-mapper boundary -- needs its own Epic/HLD, not a Story-level correction.

epicImpact.reason: Standalone, ISSUE-anchored bugfix Story with no sibling Stories; this is a correction round on this same Story's own already-approved LLD/PLAN/BUILD, not a later Story of a multi-Story Epic.
